simplicity-r1-f1.rationale: Defending R7 with cited evidence. Interview Round 4 records the user explicitly editing the AI's recommended check shape — line 50 of `004-decision-skill-interview.md`: *'edit — drop the conversation-state heuristic; the mtime-on-`task-history.json` check is sufficient and doesn't depend on harness behaviour we don't control. The soft prompt should fire when the most-recent `task-history.json` entry has a `completedAt` (or equivalent timestamp) within the last 60 minutes.'* The 60-minute number is not a magic constant the AI fabricated; it is the user's explicit specification, surfaced during grilling, with the rationale 'doesn't depend on harness behaviour we don't control' (Think-Before-Coding alignment — the user named the alternative they were rejecting). The boundary prompt is also goal-anchored: the goal's Out-of-scope-at-goal-level explicitly names 'capturing decisions tied to specific tasks (use `specflow:complete` instead)' — R7 makes that boundary visible at the user's mid-flow moment. Dropping R7 would leave the boundary documented only in the goal field and the Non-goals section, neither of which the user sees while invoking the skill. The duplicate-title check (R6) handles the same-title overlap case but does NOT handle the same-decision-different-title case (a user logs 'Postgres triggers for audit' as out-of-band right after `specflow:complete` logged 'Audit log via Postgres triggers' as a task-derived decision — both legitimate-seeming entries, but the second should have been `specflow:complete`). R7 catches that case; R6 cannot. This is interview-grounded configurability, not speculative — push back.
simplicity-r1-f1.revision_applied: R7 retained as-is (mtime check with 60-minute window, soft prompt informational only). The interview's Round 4 user-edit is the documented consumer ask; the speculative-mechanism concern does not apply when the mechanism's parameters were specified by the user during grilling.

surgical-r1-f1.rationale: Cross-skill duplication is real. Two source-of-truth locations for the canonical preamble — `specflow:setup`'s seed template and `specflow:decision`'s prompt body — would drift over time. Both proposed shapes are clean, but option (a) (refuse on file-missing) is the smaller surgical change and has the better failure mode: if `admin/decision-log.md` is missing, the project is not fully initialised and the user should run `specflow:setup` rather than have `specflow:decision` quietly seed a file the rest of the admin folder may not be ready for. Option (b) (shared template file) is correct architecturally but introduces a new `templates/decision-log-preamble.md` artefact in v1 without a documented second consumer (every other admin file's seed template lives inline in `specflow:setup`'s prompt body, not as a standalone template). Going with option (a) — refuse on file-missing.
surgical-r1-f1.revision_applied: R8 rewritten to refuse on file-missing: 'When `admin/decision-log.md` does not exist, the skill refuses to run with the message *"`admin/decision-log.md` does not exist. Run `specflow:setup` to initialise the project's admin folder first, then re-run `specflow:decision`."* The skill never seeds the file itself; `specflow:setup` is the canonical owner of admin-folder seeding.' AC-7 rewritten to verify the refusal path: 'When `admin/decision-log.md` does not exist at the start of the run, the skill refuses to write and emits the literal error *"..."*. No new entry is written; no scratch file is created.' The duplication is gone; `specflow:setup` is the single source of truth for the preamble.

tbc-r1-f1.rationale: Unstated assumption is real. 'Most-recently-written' has three plausible interpretations and the PRD silently picked one without naming it. File-order-last is the correct canonical reading order (matches what Phase 3 `/insights` consumers will see, matches the file's append-only convention) but the requirement needs to say so explicitly. The proposed edit nails the issue.
tbc-r1-f1.revision_applied: R5 edited to define 'most-recently-written existing entry' as 'the last entry in file order (i.e. the entry immediately preceding the file's final `---` separator, or the only entry in the file)' with the explicit note 'The skill does NOT use date-based ordering for this check; file order is the canonical reading order and matches what a future Phase 3 consumer will see.' AC-4's warning text updated to name file-order: *"Last entry in file order ('{title}', line {N}) contains {description of drift} — continuing with canonical schema"*. The block is resolved.

tbc-r1-f2.rationale: Missing tradeoff articulation is real. R9's parse strategy was implicit. Naming the full-file-read tradeoff explicitly with the practical-size justification is the right shape — the parse is operationally cheap on real-world decision-log files (dozens of entries per project, not thousands) and the simpler shape is the correct one. The two edge cases (head check for preamble-only, tail check for existing-entries) were both implicit; making them explicit removes the ambiguity.
tbc-r1-f2.revision_applied: R9 edited to add the read-strategy sentence: 'The parse reads the entire file — `admin/decision-log.md` is bounded in practice (decisions are dozens per project, not thousands), so a full-file read is operationally cheap and the simplest correct shape. The parse then checks (i) head: file starts with the canonical preamble; (ii) tail: file ends with either the preamble's `---` separator (no entries yet) or a complete entry + `---` separator.' AC-8's branch description updated to match.

goal-r1-f1.rationale: Reverse-traceability gap is real. The chat-line shape is a user-facing success surface (named in the goal's Success-looks-like) but it lives inside R11 as a verify-step note rather than as an R-level contract. Option (b) is the smaller surgical edit — keep R11 as the single requirement covering both stages but rephrase to make Stage 2 an R-level contract explicitly. AC-10's literal-text verification then has a stated R-level contract to verify against. Going with option (b).
goal-r1-f1.revision_applied: R11 rewritten to name Stage 2 as an R-level contract explicitly: 'Stage 1 is the binary verify step; Stage 2 is the binary user-surface contract.' The chat-line text is retained inside R11 but framed as the contract being established, not as a verify-step note. AC-10's `(Verifies R11.)` clause is unchanged but now points at a requirement that names the chat line as a contract rather than as a mechanism. The orphan-AC gap is closed.

da-r1-f1.rationale: Coverage gap on R7's edge cases is real. The file-missing case was handled at AC level via 'AND' but not named in R7's prose, and the empty-file case (recent mtime, zero entries) would fire the prompt incorrectly on any fresh project right after setup. Both cases need explicit handling. Extending R7 with both edge cases and updating AC-6's branch list to match is the right shape — small edit, both cases closed at both R and AC level.
da-r1-f1.revision_applied: R7 extended with two file-state edge cases: (i) `task-history.json` does not exist → soft prompt does not fire; (ii) `task-history.json` exists but contains zero task entries → soft prompt does not fire. AC-6 extended with the matching branch list: 'When `admin/task-history.json` does not exist, OR exists but contains zero entries, OR exists with mtime older than 3600 seconds — the prompt does not fire.'
